scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute volume is driven primarily by inadequate/slow ticket response capacity, so faster automated ticket answering is the fix (SH-CS framing).

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused more reads to be rejected or mis-substituted with estimates, producing incorrect bills.

H-AMI-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The nightly AMI export from the vendor (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or delivering incomplete/invalid reads around August, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reads (contracted to ORG-FIELD) have been incomplete or inaccurate since August, driving estimate substitution and bill errors for manually-read accounts.

H-TICKET-CLASSIFICATION-ARTIFA.statement: The apparent doubling of dispute tickets reflects a change in CRM intake/categorization rather than an actual increase in bill errors.

H-NON-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: A majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills have ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads, suggesting a cause unrelated to read/estimate substitution — e.g., tariff application or billing calculation errors — drives most of the dispute surge.

H-BILLING-CALC-ERROR.statement: Billing calculation errors unrelated to any tariff rate change (e.g., rate code misapplication, meter multiplier or consumption calculation bugs) drive most of the 59% of disputes on ACTUAL-read bills, since no tariff change occurred (E-02).

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field-reader headcount shortfall (three readers short) since July has delayed manual read routes, driving the estimate substitution and bill errors H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE attributes to incomplete manual reads.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-01 shows 3025 disputed bills split 1785 (59%) ACTUAL read type vs 1240 (41%) ESTIMATED, so a majority of disputes occur on bills with accepted, non-estimated reads. Any cause rooted purely in estimate substitution (AMI export failure, billing rule rejections, field read failure) can explain at most the 41% ESTIMATED share, not the dominant ACTUAL-read share.

billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes were logged in the billing system around the dispute-surge period. This rules out a tariff/rate change as the cause of the billing errors, including for the 59% of disputes that occur on ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads that H-NON-READ-BILL-ERROR attributed partly to tariff application errors.

E-03 shows CRM dispute volume stayed flat around 600/month in June-July (610, 590) then roughly doubled to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep), confirming the timing and magnitude of the surge but saying nothing about its cause.

E-04 shows that across 2440 dispute tickets, median response time is 1.6 days and p90 is 2.8 days, both comfortably within the 3.0-day SLA, so ticket response speed is not currently breaching service levels. The 2440-ticket count equals the Aug (1180) + Sep (1260) surge totals from E-03, indicating this dataset covers the surge period and is not itself inflated by slow handling.

E-05 shows field route completion for the 9200 manual-read accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over the 2026-08..09 period, i.e. roughly 12% of scheduled manual meter reads were not completed in the surge window. This is a plausible contributor to estimate substitution via the manual-read path but says nothing about AMI/MDMS exports, billing rules, tariffs, or ticket handling.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this non-authoritative stakeholder statement agrees with the already-recorded E-02 tariff_change_log count of zero, reinforcing (but not newly proving) that tariff rate changes are not the cause of the dispute surge.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims a reader headcount shortfall of three since July causes routes to run late, so affected customers receive estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder claim, not a measured count, and offers a specific causal mechanism (staffing) for the manual-read incompleteness already measured at 12% in E-05.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 (service contract §4.2) establishes that the utility may request field route priority changes but execution requires confirmation from the Field Operations Manager; this is a governance document about who may authorize the push_route_update action, not evidence about the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-09 provides route-level detail behind the aggregate 0.88 completion figure (E-05): 14 distinct manual-read routes each with a distinct completion value, with the sample record showing route R-00 at only 0.70 completion — well below both the 0.95 target and the 0.88 aggregate. This confirms real heterogeneity across routes but does not itself identify why any route (e.g. R-00) lags, so it cannot confirm or refute a staffing-related cause.
